evidence_used.statement: US campus paper The Pitt News quotes YouTuber Mike Chen (Strictly Dumpling): he began with Chinese traditional cultural content on Off the Great Wall before building a food-travel career.
Canadian YouTuber Trevor James (The Food Ranger), profiled by Vox, specializes in documenting Chinese street-food culture across many provinces for a primarily Western YouTube audience.
Food Ranger tells Vox he uses Mandarin and visible enthusiasm to open vendors up, aiming to show how cool Chinese food and China can be through non-political, positive food storytelling.
Australian Financial Review profiles Australian creator Amy Lyons (Blondie in China), whose China food channel has over one million followers across YouTube and other platforms.

On his overseas personal site, Trevor James says he moved to Chengdu for the food and aims to show through travel/food videos that the world is full of friendly people, countering fear-driven media narratives.
SCMP profiles Canadian creator Trevor James (The Food Ranger) for enthusiastic street-food hunting across Asia, including China-related coverage, for a large YouTube audience.

reply: Labeling grassroots cultural exchange as "propaganda" reveals a flawed geopolitical bias. Creators like Trevor James speak Mandarin to engage local vendors, highlighting China's vibrant street food and amicable citizens. Such authentic storytelling effectively dismantles fear-driven media narratives through genuine human connection. 🍜🇨🇳🌍
